is_anopheles.evidence: Studies Anopheles funestus s.s. and Anopheles arabiensis collected in southern Mozambique (page 1, Abstract; page 3, Methods).

reports_target_markers.evidence: PCR assays tested An. gambiae s.l. for Vgsc L1014F (L995F) and L1014S (L995S) and An. funestus for Cyp6p9a RFLP (Cyp6p9a R) (page 4, 'Insecticide resistance molecular detection').

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Page 7, 'Molecular resistance': 'Of the 164 An. arabiensis that were tested for the 1014 locus of the kdr gene that confers pyrethroid resistance, 162 (98.8%) were homozygous susceptible and 2 (1.2%) did not amplify... Of the 420 An. funestus s.s. mosquitoes, 408 had enough DNA extract available for the CYP6P9a gene detection PCR for pyrethroid resistance. 401 (98.3%) were homozygous resistant, one was heterozygous resistant (0.2%), two were homozygous susceptible (0.5%), and four (1.0%) did not amplify.'

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected as adults inside houses in 11 towns across Maputo and Gaza provinces in southern Mozambique between March and May 2016 (page 3, 'Mosquito collection').

is_primary_study.evidence: Primary empirical research paper reporting field collections, CDC bottle bioassays, and molecular genotyping.

sub_country_location.evidence: 11 towns across Manhiça, Magude, and Bilene districts: Bobole, Buna, Chobela, Ilha Josina, Macia, Magude (Mulelemani), Maragra, Palmeira (and 8 specific bairros within Palmeira), Punguene, Ribangua, and 3 de Fevereiro (page 3, Fig. 1 and text).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from March 9 to May 4, 2016 (page 3, 'Mosquito collection').

duplicate_risk.evidence: Field collections were conducted specifically for this study by the authors in collaboration with CISM in 2016, with no mention of re-used external genomic datasets.

supplement.evidence: Bioassay data per locality (counts, sample sizes, and mortalities) are in Additional file 1: Tables S1, S2, and S3: '30-min mortality rates at 1x diagnostic dose ranging from 3.9% (Buna) to 88.8% (Ilha Josina) (Additional file 1: Table S1, Fig. 3A)' (page 6).

assessment.summary: This study evaluated deltamethrin susceptibility via CDC bottle bioassays and genotyped Vgsc L1014F/S in An. arabiensis (n=164, 162 SS, 2 failed) and Cyp6p9a R via RFLP in An. funestus s.s. (n=408, 401 RR, 1 RS, 2 SS, 4 failed) collected from 11 towns in southern Mozambique in 2016.
